title: Power supply to remain uninterrupted: Nalinda
byline: The government will not resort to power cuts, Cabinet Spokesperson and Minister of Health and Mass Media Nalinda Jayatissa said.

title: “Ehipassiko” peace march reaches third day, proceeds towards Kandy
byline: The third day of the “Ehipassiko” peace march commenced this morning (23) at the historic Aluvihara Raja Maha Vihara.

title: Nalinda justifies politicians earning assets
byline: In the wake of controversy surrounding accumulation of assets by ministers, Cabinet Spokesman Minister Nalinda Jayatissa said yesterday assets earned by politicians are not an issue as long as they can reveal how they were earned.

title: Drug price hike around the corner
byline: Drug prices in Sri Lanka are set to increase in the near future with authorities considering a revision of existing price controls amid mounting pressure from importers grappling with rising global costs and a weakening rupee.

title: Sri Lanka chooses Chinese currency to pay for Russian oil transactions
byline: Sri Lanka, which is planning to purchase crude oil from Russia, has agreed to settle payments in Chinese Renminbi (RMB), newly appointed Energy Minister Aruna Karunatilake said.

title: Iran says Strait of Hormuz cannot be opened due to ceasefire breaches
byline: Iran’s chief negotiator in talks with the US said it is ’’not possible’’ for the Strait of Hormuz to be opened due to ’’the blatant violations of the ceasefire’’ by the US and Israel.

title: US Navy chief leaving post ’effective immediately’, Pentagon says
byline: US Navy Secretary John Phelan is leaving the Trump administration, the Pentagon announced on Wednesday.

title: US intercepts three Iranian oil tankers in Asian waters, sources say
byline: The U.S. military has intercepted at least three Iranian-flagged tankers in ‌Asian waters and is redirecting them away from their positions near India, Malaysia and Sri Lanka, shipping and security sources said on Wednesday.

title: Deputy Minister escapes unhurt in accident
byline: The vehicle carrying Deputy Minister of Education and Higher Education, Dr. Madura Seneviratne, was involved in an accident on Tuesday night (22).

title: China’s Xpeng expects to start delivering ’flying’ cars in 2027
byline: Chinese electric vehicle maker Xpeng (9868.HK), expects to start large-scale ​production of its ’’flying’’ cars next year and of its humanoid robots in ‌the fourth quarter of 2026, President Brian Gu told Reuters on Thursday.

title: Hackers also attempted to obtain funds linked to payment to India: Deputy Minister
byline: Deputy Minister of Finance Dr. Anil Jayantha said that the hackers who had fraudulently obtained funds to be made to the Australian Export Finance Agency, had also attempted to obtain funds associated with a payment to be made to India as well.

title: Krrish deal case against Namal fixed for May
byline: The case against Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa over the alleged Krrish deal was today fixed for May 29 by the Colombo High Court.

title: Trump envoy seeks to replace Iran with Italy in football World Cup
byline: An envoy to Donald Trump has asked FIFA to replace Iran with Italy in the upcoming World Cup, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday.

title: Rupee slides further as dollar selling rate hits Rs. 321
byline: The Sri Lankan rupee weakened further against the US dollar across commercial banks today (23), with the selling rate reaching Rs. 321.

title: Air India mulls broad flight cuts amid high fuel costs
byline: Tata Group-owned Air India is weighing a significant scale-back of its flight operations after reportedly posting a loss of nearly Rs 20,000 crore in FY26, amid persistent operational headwinds and elevated aviation fuel costs, businessline newspaper reported on Thursday quoting industry sources.

title: Middle East conflict hits Sri Lanka tourism, arrivals down 20%
byline: The ongoing conflict in the Middle East is negatively affecting Sri Lanka’s tourism industry, particularly as the peak tourist season approaches, Tourism Deputy Minister and MP Ruwan Ranasinghe said.

title: New Year holiday closure causes temporary drop in egg prices, industry says
byline: The closure of shops and bakeries during the Sinhala and Hindu New Year period has led to a temporary decline in egg prices, Egg Producers Association Treasurer Wijaya Alwis said.

title: Stranded conductor found during major inspection in Colombo
byline: A routine inspection in Colombo took an unusual turn this morning when a bus conductor was found left behind after his own bus reportedly drove off without him.

title: Let Parliament decide on probe on hacking of dollars 2.5 million: Free Lawyers
byline: Whilst revealing that a sum of US dollars 2.5 million which the government sent to a certain donor as a payment of an installment has been hacked on December 31 last year, the Free Lawyers Organisation yesterday urged Speaker to get Parliament to come up with a proper investigation mechanism.

title: Demand for premium number plates surges past 1,100 since 2023
byline: The number of motorists opting for high-value vehicle number plates has increased significantly, with over 1,100 plates either issued or reserved since 2023, officials told the Parliamentary Committee on Public Finance (COPF).

title: Personalized vehicle number plates planned following system upgrade
byline: The Department of Motor Traffic (DMT) is planning to introduce personalized vehicle number plates featuring customers name, once its existing system is upgraded, officials informed the Parliamentary Committee on Public Finance (COPF).

title: Court dismisses cricketer Thushara’s NOC plaint following withdrawal
byline: Sri Lankan cricketer Nuwan Thushara today withdrew the plaint he had filed before the Colombo District Court seeking an interim injunction compelling Sri Lanka Cricket to issue him a “No Objection Certificate” to enable his participation in the 2026 Indian Premier League (IPL) and other international premier league tournaments.

title: Trump says Iran won’t execute 8 women after he demanded their release
byline: President Trump announced Wednesday that Iran will no longer execute eight women after he pleaded Tuesday for their freedom — calling it “very good news” in a social media post.

title: Iran FM discusses IRIS Dena attack with Sri Lanka, seeks justice
byline: Iran’s Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi said during a telephone conversation with Sri Lanka’s Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath that Iran will take all legal and political means to hold the perpetrators and those responsible accountable and bring them to justice over the attack on the IRIS Dena off the coast of Sri Lanka.

title: Submerged ruins resurface as Maussakelle water levels drop
byline: The rapid decline in water levels at the Maussakelle Reservoir has exposed remnants of the old Maskeliya town, long submerged beneath its waters.

title: Peter Hill to return to SriLankan Airlines as next Chairman this week?
byline: SriLankan Airlines is bracing for a highly contentious leadership overhaul at its upcoming board meeting scheduled for this Saturday, April 25.

title: Qatar Airways resumes daily Dubai, Sharjah flights as UAE travel links restored
byline: Travellers in the UAE will once again have more flight options as Qatar Airways resumes daily services to Dubai and Sharjah from April 23, marking a key step in restoring regional connectivity.

title: MK Stalin, Vijay, EPS face high-stakes battles in key Tamil Nadu seats
byline: The electoral battlelines are drawn, and voting day is here in Tamil Nadu, which goes to the polls in a single phase on April 23. The ruling DMK – in alliance with Congress and DMDK – faces AIADMK, which has tied up with BJP and PMK.

title: Australia assisting probe into payment issues
byline: The Australian High Commission in Colombo said that it is aware of irregularities related to payments owed to the Australian Government, according to a statement posted on X.

title: Complaint lodged with IGP over alleged misdirection of USD 2.5 million Treasury payment
byline: A complaint has been lodged with the Inspector General of Police calling for an immediate investigation into an alleged misdirection of a USD 2.5 million payment made by the Sri Lankan Treasury.

title: Iran tightens control of Hormuz after US calls off renewed attacks
byline: Iran seized two ships in the Strait of Hormuz as it tightened its grip on the strategic waterway after U.S. President Donald Trump announced he was indefinitely calling ​off attacks, with no sign of peace talks restarting.

title: Sri Lanka’s first Online Safety Act case concludes before Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court
byline: In a landmark development, the Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court today made permanent its conditional order against two respondents in the first-ever case filed under Sri Lanka’s Online Safety Act No. 9 of 2024.

title: FSP back in Yakkala office after court intervention
byline: The Frontline Socialist Party (FSP) today resumed operations at its Yakkala office in the Gampaha District following a court order directing the Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna (JVP) to hand over the premises.

title: Hacking of USD 2.5 million – Public could lose trust on banks: Joint opposition
byline: The people of Sri Lanka will lose trust on banks as a result of the hacking of the USD 2.5 million government funds, the Joint Opposition said today.

title: Amber advisory issued for severe lightning across several provinces
byline: The Meteorology Department has issued an Amber advisory warning of severe lightning conditions expected in several parts of the country, valid until 11.30 p.m. today.

title: Police warn of fake SriLankan Airlines scam targeting bank accounts
byline: The Police have issued an urgent warning regarding a sophisticated financial fraud operation impersonating the national carrier, SriLankan Airlines.

title: Public urged not to distract ‘Walk for Peace’ procession as dog falls ill
byline: The dog accompanying the “Walk for Peace” procession fell ill yesterday after being affected by heavy crowds and disruptions, and required medical treatment.

title: SLIATE union begins strike over longstanding issues
byline: The Academics’ Union of the Sri Lanka Institute of Advanced Technological Education has decided to launch trade union action from today after more than 15 years of unsuccessful attempts to resolve longstanding issues through discussions with relevant authorities.

title: China’s Xpeng expects to start delivering ’flying’ cars in 2027
byline: Chinese electric vehicle maker Xpeng (9868.HK), expects to start large-scale ​production of its ’’flying’’ cars next year and of its humanoid robots in ‌the fourth quarter of 2026, President Brian Gu told Reuters on Thursday.

title: Air India mulls broad flight cuts amid high fuel costs
byline: Tata Group-owned Air India is weighing a significant scale-back of its flight operations after reportedly posting a loss of nearly Rs 20,000 crore in FY26, amid persistent operational headwinds and elevated aviation fuel costs, businessline newspaper reported on Thursday quoting industry sources.

title: Market remains rangebound amid geopolitical uncertainty
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange ended the session on a subdued note, with both indices posting marginal losses as uncertainty surrounding the Middle East conflict continued to cloud investor sentiment. With no clear directional cues emerging, the market opened in a stalemate and remained largely rangebound throughout the day.

title: Deadline for 2026 GCE A/L applications ends tonight
byline: The Examinations Department announced that the deadline for submitting applications for the General Certificate of Education (GCE ) Advanced Level Examination (A/L) Examination 2026 falls at 12:00 midnight tomorrow (24).

title: US forces board sanctioned ship in Indian Ocean, defence department says
byline: US forces have interdicted a sanctioned vessel that is transporting oil from Iran, the country’s defence department has posted on X.

title: Young man remanded for secretly filming bathing neighbour
byline: A man who had allegedly recorded a video of a neighbouring woman while she was bathing and had sent it to one of her friends was ordered to be remanded till May 4 by Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama today.

title: Trump orders Navy to ‘shoot and kill any boat’ laying mines in Hormuz Strait
byline: President Donald Trump on Thursday said he has ordered the U.S. Navy “to shoot and kill any boat” that is laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Lebanon to seek ceasefire extension in U.S.-hosted talks with Israel
byline: The ​U.S. will host a second meeting between Lebanese and Israeli envoys on Thursday (April 23, 2026), with Beirut seeking the ‌extension of a ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah, a day after Israeli strikes ​killed at least five people including a journalist.

title: Applications deadline for ‘Presidential Environment Awards – 2026’ extended to May 15
byline: The Central Environmental Authority (CEA) has announced an extension of the application deadline for the “Presidential Environment Awards – 2026” programme until May 15, 2026, following requests from prospective applicants.

title: Trump administration reclassifies cannabis as less dangerous
byline: The US Department of Justice has officially reclassified cannabis as less dangerous, marking a major shift in the country’s drug policy.

title: Sri Lanka–UN talks focus on Haiti troop deployment standards
byline: Discussions on the prospective deployment of Sri Lankan troops to Haiti under the proposed Gang Suppression Force (GSF), with a strong focus on operational readiness, compliance with UN standards, and adherence to human rights requirements, took centre stage during high-level talks between Sri Lanka and the United Nations in New York.

title: Govt reviews plan to place retiring sailors in global maritime jobs
byline: Review progress on expanding foreign employment opportunities for retiring Sri Lanka Navy (SLN) personnel in the shipping and marine sector was the focus of a follow-up discussion held at the Office of the Deputy Minister of Defence in Colombo.

title: Deadline for 2026 GCE A/L applications ends tomorrow
byline: The Examinations Department announced that the deadline for submitting applications for the General Certificate of Education (GCE ) Advanced Level Examination (A/L) Examination 2026 falls at 12:00 midnight tomorrow (24).
